input.rationale: Section 13.5 correctly gives us ownership of Developments (software interface coding and programs created solely by Corio) and includes an assignment from Commerce One, but the carve-out flips ownership of our own work product to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports those Developments on an ongoing basis. That is an assignment of Customer IP to the Vendor, which is our walk-away position, and support arrangements should be handled by licence rather than title. The agreement also contains no statement that we and our Customers retain rights in data hosted on the Corio Servers or passing through the MarketSite.net Service (Section 10 only cross-refers to an NDA), so we added a short Customer Data ownership and no-joint-ownership confirmation. Commerce One's retained ownership of the Software under Section 2.8 is untouched and acceptable.

ops.oldText: shall be owned by Corio, unless such Developments are supported on an ongoing basis by Commerce One in which case Commerce One will retain all ownership rights, including
ops.newText: shall be owned by Corio, including

ops.text: Corio and its Customers shall retain all right, title and interest in and to all data and content submitted to, processed by or stored in the Software, the MarketSite.net Service or the Corio Servers ("CUSTOMER DATA"). No right, title or interest in any Customer Data or in any other Corio intellectual property is assigned or transferred to Commerce One under this Agreement, and nothing in this Agreement creates joint ownership of any Developments or Customer Data.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have deleted the carve-out that would hand Commerce One ownership of Developments created solely by Corio merely because Commerce One supports them on an ongoing basis, and added a short confirmation that Corio and its Customers retain all rights in Customer Data with no assignment to Commerce One and no joint ownership. Our position is that we own what we build and pay for while Commerce One keeps its pre-existing Software rights (Section 2.8); if ongoing support is the concern, we can instead grant Commerce One a licence to the relevant Developments for support purposes.
proposal.summary: Remove vendor ownership carve-out over Corio-created Developments and confirm Corio/Customer retain all rights in Customer Data, with no assignment or joint ownership.
